mainTopic: Changing how one carries on יום טוב, staying silent when people will not listen, and whether one may start using a storeroom (מוקצה)
overview: This amud opens with the end of the משנה: on יום טוב you may start taking straw from a pile, but not wood from the מוקצה storage yard. The גמרא quotes a ברייתא: if changing the normal way of carrying is impossible, it is permitted. רבא applies this in מחוזא with a ladder of changes for each kind of carrier, plus an exception when no change is possible. רב אשי explains that women may carry water jugs normally, because every possible change would create a new problem. Next, the גמרא asks why no one stops people from clapping and dancing on יום טוב. The answer is the famous rule מוטב שיהיו שוגגין ואל יהיו מזידין: if people will not listen, it is better to stay silent. The גמרא shows this applies even to Torah laws, using the example of תוספת יום הכפורים. Finally, רב כהנא draws a rule about starting to use a storeroom from the משנה, in two opposite versions. In one version the משנה follows רבי שמעון; in the other it follows רבי יהודה, with the straw explained as rotten and thorny.

steps.title: End of the משנה: straw pile allowed, stored wood not
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends by allowing one to start using a pile of straw on יום טוב, but not wood kept in the מוקצה storage area.
steps.simpleTranslation: [One may begin to take] from a pile of straw, but not from the wood that is in the storage yard.
steps.whatsHappening: These are the closing words of the משנה. The full sentence (begun on the previous page) says you may start taking from a straw pile on יום טוב, but not from wood in the back storage yard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A straw pile counts as ready for use even though no one set it aside before יום טוב. Wood in the מוקצה yard is stored away for the long term, so the owner has put it out of his mind. That makes it מוקצה and off-limits.

keyTerms.meaning: here: a storage yard behind the house for things not meant for use soon; such items are set aside and forbidden to handle

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a sentence. The verb 'one may begin' (וּמַתְחִילִין) came just before, on the previous page.

phrases.english: [one may begin to take] from the pile of straw,
phrases.notes: Continues 'ומתחילין' from the previous page of the משנה.

phrases.english: but not from the wood that is in the storage yard.
phrases.notes: Wood stored long-term is mentally set aside, so it is מוקצה.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּעֲרֵמַת הַתֶּבֶן אֲבָל לֹא בָּעֵצִים שֶׁבַּמּוּקְצֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closing line of the משנה, continued from the previous page.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A straw pile may be started on יום טוב; wood in the מוקצה storage yard may not.

steps.title: ברייתא: if changing is impossible, it is permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites a ברייתא: the משנה's rule to carry differently on יום טוב does not apply when changing is impossible.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: A תנא taught: If it is impossible to change [the normal way], it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by quoting a ברייתא. It adds an exception to the משנה's rule that you must carry things differently on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the משנה said not to carry jugs of wine in a basket the normal weekday way, but to change the method (שינוי). The ברייתא adds a limit: if no change is possible, you may carry the normal way. This might be because of the type of object, or because there is no time.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule becomes the source that רבא relies on in the next steps, and the גמרא quotes it word for word again there.

phrases.english: Gemara: A Tanna taught:
phrases.notes: Start of the גמרא; quoting a ברייתא.

phrases.english: If it is impossible to change, it is permitted.
phrases.notes: Refers to the required change in carrying from the משנה on the previous page.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא אִם אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְשַׁנּוֹת מוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא by adding a ברייתא that limits the משנה's rule on changing how one carries.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When change is impossible, carrying in the normal weekday way on יום טוב is permitted.

steps.title: רבא's ladder of changes in Mechoza
steps.stepSummary: רבא set up a graded system in מחוזא: each type of carrier moves one level away from his usual method on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא instituted in מחוזא: One who carries with difficulty should carry on a pitchfork. One who carries on a pitchfork should carry on a pole on two people's shoulders. One who carries on a shoulder-pole should carry on a pole held in the hands. One who carries on a pole in the hands should spread a scarf over it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא makes a practical rule for his city, מחוזא. Each person must change his normal weekday way of carrying on יום טוב, and the change depends on how he usually carries.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is not to make carrying easier or harder. It is to make it look different from weekday work, so everyone sees it is יום טוב. Even the last level, a pole carried in the hands, still gets a change: you cover the load with a scarf.

keyTerms.meaning: a carrying pole on two people's shoulders
a carrying pole held in the hands

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the goal is to make carrying harder. One level (shoulder pole to hand pole) isn't easier or harder. The point is only that it looks different from a weekday.

phrases.english: Rava instituted in Mechoza:
Those who carry with difficulty should carry on a pitchfork.
Those who carry on a pitchfork should carry on a carrying pole on the shoulders.
phrases.notes: Held by two people.

phrases.english: Those who carry on a shoulder-pole should carry on a pole in the hands.
Those who carry on a pole in the hands should spread a scarf over it,
phrases.notes: סודרא = scarf/cloth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Puts the principle of שינוי into a practical system for a whole city.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each carrier on יום טוב must move one step away from his usual weekday method; the final level covers the load with a scarf.

steps.title: רבא's exception, based on the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבא adds that if no change is possible, carrying normally is allowed. He bases this on the ברייתא quoted earlier.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it is not possible, it is permitted, as the Master said: If it is impossible to change, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his rule with an exception: when changing is not possible, you may carry normally. The גמרא shows that his source is the ברייתא from step 2.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This links the practical rule back to its source. The words 'דאמר מר' bring the ברייתא again word for word, this time as proof for רבא's exception. So the city-wide system has a built-in limit.

keyTerms.meaning: as the Master said; cites an earlier source

steps.whatToRemember: The rule of שינוי on יום טוב: change your normal way of carrying as much as you can, but if change is impossible, it is permitted (from the ברייתא, applied by רבא).

phrases.english: And if it is not possible, it is permitted.
phrases.notes: Because of the object or because there is no time.

phrases.english: As the Master said:
phrases.notes: Points back to the ברייתא.

phrases.english: If it is impossible to change, it is permitted.
phrases.notes: Word-for-word repeat of the ברייתא, now used as a source.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם לָא אֶפְשָׁר שְׁרֵי דְּאָמַר מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's rule with its exception and ties it to the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If no change is possible, normal carrying is permitted, based on the ברייתא.

steps.title: Why don't women carrying water jugs have to change?
steps.stepSummary: רב חנן בר רבא challenges רב אשי: the rule is to change whenever possible, yet women fill water jugs on יום טוב the normal way and no one objects.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנן בר רבא said to רב אשי: The Sages said that as much as it is possible to change, we change on יום טוב. But these women fill their jugs with water on יום טוב and do not change, and we say nothing to them!
steps.whatsHappening: רב חנן בר רבא points out a problem with the rule. Women draw water in jugs the normal weekday way on יום טוב, and no one tells them to change.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Changing a water jug's carrying style is clearly possible, so the 'impossible' exception does not seem to apply. Yet common practice allows it without protest. The question is either why the rule is not enforced here, or whether the practice is wrong. The answer comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: and we don't say anything at all to them

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חָנָן בַּר רָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Chanan bar Rava said to Rav Ashi:
The Sages said:
phrases.notes: States the rule before challenging it.

phrases.english: as much as it is possible to change,
we change on Yom Tov.
But look at these women
phrases.notes: וְהָא signals the challenge.

phrases.aramaic: דְּקָא מָלְיָין חַצְבַיְיהוּ מַיָּא בְּיוֹמָא טָבָא,
phrases.english: who fill their jugs with water on Yom Tov,
and they do not change,
and we do not say anything at all to them!
phrases.notes: Common practice seems to contradict the rule.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא הָנֵי נְשֵׁי דְּקָא מָלְיָין חַצְבַיְיהוּ מַיָּא בְּיוֹמָא טָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the שינוי rule from step 3 by pointing to a common practice that ignores it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that one must change the normal way of carrying on יום טוב whenever possible.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Women carry water jugs normally on יום טוב, change is possible, and no one objects. This seems to go against the required שינוי.

steps.title: No change is possible for the water jugs
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the women cannot change how they carry the jugs, because every possible change creates a new problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is because a change is not possible. How should she do it? If she usually fills a large jug, should she fill a small jug? Then she adds extra walking. If she usually fills a small jug, should she fill a large jug? Then she adds to her load. Should she cover the jug with a lid? Sometimes the lid falls, and she will come to carry it. Should she tie the lid on? Sometimes the rope snaps, and she will come to tie it again. Should she spread a cloth over the jug? Sometimes the cloth gets soaked in water, and she will come to squeeze it. So a change is not possible.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the challenge from Step 5. The women are not ignoring the rule. In their case, a change is simply impossible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי tests every way the women could change their carrying, and each one fails. A smaller or larger jug adds walking or weight. A lid, a tied lid, or a cloth each risk a real איסור: carrying the fallen lid, tying a knot, or סחיטה (squeezing). This fits the ברייתא from Step 2 exactly: when a change is impossible, carrying the normal way is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: She increases (her walking or her load)
Squeezing liquid out of a cloth, a forbidden מלאכה

steps.whatToRemember: The rule to carry differently on יום טוב applies only when the change does not create a new problem. For the water jugs, every change does create one, so the women may carry the normal way.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the rule to change one's usual method is a fence for protection. It does not apply when the change itself would lead to a bigger problem.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is because it is not possible.
phrases.notes: רב אשי answers רב חנן בר רבא.

phrases.english: How should she act?
One who usually fills a large jug,
should she fill a small jug?
Then she increases her walking.
phrases.notes: She would need more trips to bring the same amount of water.

phrases.english: One who usually fills a small jug,
should she fill a large jug?
Then she increases her load.
Should she cover it with a lid?
Sometimes it falls, and she will come to carry it.
phrases.notes: She would carry the fallen lid by hand, like a burden.

phrases.english: Should she tie it on?
Sometimes it snaps, and she will come to tie it again.
phrases.notes: Tying a knot is a forbidden מלאכה.

phrases.english: Should she spread a cloth over it?
Sometimes it gets soaked in the water,
and she will come to squeezing.
Therefore, it is not possible.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from Step 5 about the women's water jugs.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applying a known exception: the case falls under the rule that when no change is possible, carrying normally is allowed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The women break the rule to change their carrying, and no one protests.
steps.terutzMaskana: Every possible change creates a new risk, so no change is possible, and the normal method is permitted.

steps.title: Clapping and dancing are forbidden, yet people do it
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר רב חנין asks אביי: the משנה forbids clapping and dancing on יום טוב, yet people do it and no one objects.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר רב חנין said to אביי: We learned in a משנה: One may not clap, nor slap one's thigh, nor dance on יום טוב. But nowadays we see that women do these things, and we do not say anything to them!
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge begins. רבא בר רב חנין points to a clear rule in the משנה that people openly break, while no one stops them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is unlike the water jugs. Here a change is clearly possible, because people could simply not clap or dance. So the answer 'it is not possible' does not work here. The question is why no one protests against a clear גזירה of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Slapping one's hand on one's thigh
And we do not say anything to them

steps.confusionAlert: The reason for this גזירה is not that clapping is a מלאכה. The fear is that people may come to fix a musical instrument.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא בַּר רַב חָנִין לְאַבָּיֵי,
phrases.english: Rava bar Rav Chanin said to Abaye:
We learned in a mishna: One may not clap,
nor slap the thigh, nor dance.
phrases.notes: This is a rabbinic decree, made out of concern that one may come to fix musical instruments.

phrases.english: But nowadays we see that they do so,
and we do not say anything to them?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא בַּר רַב חָנִין לְאַבָּיֵי, תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same pattern as Step 5 (people do it and no one objects), but in a case where a change is clearly possible.
steps.kashyaTarget: The practice of not protesting when people clap and dance on יום טוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה forbids these actions, and refraining is easy. So why does no one stop people from doing them?

steps.title: אביי points to another case where no one protests
steps.stepSummary: אביי replies that by the same logic, one could ask about women sitting at the alleyway entrance, which רבא forbade, yet no one protests.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: And according to your reasoning, what about what רבא said: A person should not sit at the entrance of an alleyway, by the side post, because an object might roll away from him, and he will come to carry it four cubits in the public domain. But these women take their jugs, go, and sit at the entrance of the alleyway, and we do not say anything to them!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי does not answer directly yet. He points out that the same 'problem' exists in another, even more serious case. This is setting up the principle the גמרא will state next to explain why no one protests.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The alleyway case involves a risk of carrying four אמות in רשות הרבים, which is a Torah-level איסור. Even so, no one protests when the women sit there. If that is accepted, then not protesting against clapping and dancing, which is only a rabbinic decree, is not surprising. Both cases call for one shared explanation, which the גמרא will give next.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning: a reply that turns the question back on the asker
A side post placed at the edge of an alleyway to make it a private domain

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying the women are acting properly. He is showing that the question applies equally to another case, so both need the same explanation.

phrases.english: He said to him: And according to your reasoning,
what about that which (Rava) said:
A person should not sit at the entrance by the side post,
lest an object roll away from him,
and he will come to carry it (four cubits in the public domain).
But these women take their jugs,
and go and sit at the entrance of the alleyway,
and we do not say anything to them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to Step 7 by showing that the same question applies to an even more serious case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Parallel case: the asker's question is widened, setting up a shared principle that explains both cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Not protesting against clapping and dancing is a unique problem that needs its own explanation.
steps.terutzMaskana: Not protesting happens even with a Torah-level risk, so a general principle about not protesting must be at work. The גמרא states it next.

steps.title: Better to leave people as unknowing sinners
steps.stepSummary: אביי finishes his answer. We do not protest because it is better that people sin unknowingly than deliberately, and the same applies to clapping and dancing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the rule is: leave the Jewish people alone. It is better that they sin by mistake than sin on purpose. Here too, with clapping and dancing, leave them alone. It is better that they sin by mistake than on purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי now gives the real reason no one protests. If people will not listen anyway, warning them only turns their mistake into a deliberate sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 8 אביי showed that the question about clapping also applies to רבא's ruling on women at the alleyway, which no one enforces either. Here he gives one rule that answers both cases: if rebuke will not work, stay silent. The silence does not make the act permitted. It only keeps the sin at the lighter level of שוגג.

keyTerms.meaning: Leave the Jewish people alone (do not rebuke them)
Unintentional sinners, who do not know it is forbidden
Intentional sinners, who know and do it anyway

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean clapping and dancing become permitted. The act is still forbidden. The rule is only about whether to rebuke people who will not listen.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule, מוטב שיהיו שוגגין, is a famous guideline for when to stay silent about others' sins.

phrases.english: Rather: leave the Jewish people alone,
it is better that they be unintentional sinners
and not be intentional sinners.
Here too: leave the Jewish people alone,
phrases.notes: Applies the rule to clapping and dancing.

phrases.english: it is better that they be unintentional sinners
and not be intentional sinners.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's answer from Step 8 by stating the principle behind the silence.
steps.terutzResolutionType: General principle explaining why no one protests
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Silence suggests that clapping and dancing are permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: Silence comes from the rule that people who will not listen are better left as שוגגין. The act is still forbidden.

steps.title: Proposed limit: only for rabbinic prohibitions
steps.stepSummary: Some suggested that this rule of silence applies only to rabbinic laws, not Torah laws.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this rule applies only to rabbinic laws. But for Torah laws, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a view that limits the rule of silence to rabbinic prohibitions. It is setting this up so it can be rejected in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that a Torah sin is serious enough that we must protest even if people may not listen. Clapping and dancing are only rabbinic, so we stay silent there.

keyTerms.meaning: And these words apply only to (a limiting formula)

phrases.english: And these words apply to rabbinic laws,
but for Torah laws, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָנֵי מִילֵּי בִּדְרַבָּנַן, אֲבָל בִּדְאוֹרָיְיתָא לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes a limit on the rule from Step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Proposed: the rule of silence applies only to rabbinic prohibitions.

steps.title: Rejected: the rule applies to Torah laws too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the limit. People eat on ערב יום כיפור into the Torah-required extra time, and we say nothing to them.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not so. Whether it is a Torah law or a rabbinic law, we do not say anything to them. For adding time to יום כיפור is a Torah law, and people eat and drink until dark, and we say nothing to them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the idea from Step 10 and proves that the rule of silence covers Torah laws as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah requires adding some time before יום כיפור begins, called תוספת יום הכפורים. Many people eat right up until dark, which violates a Torah law, yet no one rebukes them. So the rule of silence does not depend on how serious the law is. It depends only on whether people will listen.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is not so (rejecting a previous view)
Adding extra time to the start of יום כיפור

steps.whatToRemember: מוטב שיהיו שוגגין applies to Torah and rabbinic laws alike. When people will not listen, we stay silent.

phrases.english: But it is not so;
there is no difference whether by Torah law
or by rabbinic law,
we do not say anything to them,
for the extension of יום כיפור
is a Torah law,
and people eat and drink until dark,
and we do not say anything to them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא הִיא, לָא שְׁנָא בִּדְאוֹרָיְיתָא וְלָא שְׁנָא בִּדְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the limit proposed in Step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Full rejection of the claim that the rule applies only to rabbinic laws.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Everyday practice shows silence even about a Torah law, תוספת יום הכפורים.

steps.title: רב כהנא: one may start taking from a storeroom
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה. רב כהנא learns from 'one may begin a straw pile' that one may start using a storeroom on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: and one may begin taking from a pile of straw. רב כהנא said: this teaches that one may begin taking from a storeroom in the first place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה, and רב כהנא draws a rule from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A straw pile set aside for storage could seem 'put out of mind' and so forbidden on יום טוב. Since the משנה allows starting to take from it, רב כהנא concludes that any storeroom of goods may be opened and used on יום טוב, even if it was not used before.

keyTerms.meaning: This teaches (an inference from a source)
In the first place, beginning fresh

phrases.english: And one may begin taking from a pile of straw.
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה.

phrases.english: רב כהנא said:
This teaches
that one may begin taking from a storeroom in the first place.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַתְחִילִין בַּעֲרֵמַת הַתֶּבֶן. אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא: זֹאת אוֹמֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section analyzing a different line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may begin taking from a storeroom on יום טוב.

steps.title: This follows רבי שמעון, who rejects מוקצה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא identifies the author of this part of the משנה as רבי שמעון, who does not hold of מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? It is רבי שמעון, who does not hold of מוקצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whose opinion this line follows and answers right away: רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Opening a storeroom on יום טוב is allowed only if we do not treat stored items as 'set aside.' That fits רבי שמעון, who does not forbid things just because a person had them out of mind before the holiday.

keyTerms.meaning: Items set aside and not prepared for use on שבת or יום טוב

phrases.english: Whose view is this? It is רבי שמעון,
who does not hold of מוקצה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies the author of the rule drawn in Step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא this line of the משנה follows.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי שמעון, who does not hold of מוקצה.

steps.title: The end of the משנה sounds like רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends by forbidding wood from the storage area, which sounds like רבי יהודה, who does hold of מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Look at the end of the משנה: but not wood from the storage area. So now we are following רבי יהודה, who does hold of מוקצה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges Step 13. If the start of the משנה follows רבי שמעון, why does the end forbid stored wood?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Forbidding stored wood looks like a מוקצה ruling, which matches רבי יהודה. It is a problem for one משנה to switch authors from its start to its end, so this attacks the claim that the משנה follows רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: Look at the end section of the source
We have arrived at (the view of)

phrases.english: Say the end of the משנה:
but not wood in the storage area.
We have come to רבי יהודה,
who does hold of מוקצה!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא סֵיפָא: אֲבָל לֹא בָּעֵצִים שֶׁבַּמּוּקְצֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim in Step 13 that the משנה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The end of the משנה forbids stored wood, which is a מוקצה ruling, so the end seems to follow רבי יהודה.

steps.title: Expensive cedar wood: even רבי שמעון agrees
steps.stepSummary: The wood in the משנה is costly cedar and fir. It is מוקצה because of money loss, and even רבי שמעון agrees to that.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here we are dealing with cedar and fir wood, which is מוקצה because of money loss, and even רבי שמעון agrees.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The forbidden wood is a special kind that even רבי שמעון treats as מוקצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cedar and fir are expensive building materials. A person deliberately keeps them away from use so he will not lose money. This kind of מוקצה, called מוקצה מחמת חסרון כיס, is accepted even by רבי שמעון, so the whole משנה can follow him.

keyTerms.meaning: Cedars and firs, expensive building wood
Set aside because using it would cause money loss

steps.whatToRemember: In the first version of רב כהנא's teaching, the whole משנה follows רבי שמעון. He rejects ordinary מוקצה but agrees to מוקצה מחמת חסרון כיס. (The second version, in Step 16, reads the whole משנה as רבי יהודה.)
steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון does not reject every kind of מוקצה. He agrees that items kept away from use because of their value are forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the important category of מוקצה מחמת חסרון כיס, which is accepted even by those who are lenient about מוקצה.

phrases.english: Here we are dealing with cedars and firs,
which are מוקצה because of money loss,
and even רבי שמעון agrees.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 14 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Forbidding stored wood shows the משנה holds of general מוקצה, like רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The wood is expensive, so it is מוקצה מחמת חסרון כיס, which even רבי שמעון forbids. The whole משנה follows רבי שמעון.

steps.title: Second version: רב כהנא learns from the end of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: Some teach רב כהנא's statement on the סיפא: from 'but not wood from the storage area' he learns that one may not begin using a storeroom on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some people teach רב כהנא's statement on the last part of the משנה, 'but not wood from the storage area.' רב כהנא said: This teaches that one may not start taking from a storeroom on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of רב כהנא's teaching. Here he learns from the end of the משנה instead of the beginning, and he reaches the opposite rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version (Step 12), רב כהנא learned from the straw pile that one MAY start using a storeroom. In this version he learns from the wood that one may NOT start using a storeroom. The same משנה gives two opposite rules, depending on which part of it you treat as the main case.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who teach it (a second version of the same statement)
The last part (end clause) of a משנה
Wood in the storage area, set aside and not meant for use
This teaches us (a rule learned from the text)
A storeroom of goods put away for long-term storage

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new statement by רב כהנא. It is a different report of the same statement from Step 12. The two versions reach OPPOSITE conclusions about starting to use a storeroom on יום טוב.

phrases.english: There are those who teach it on the latter clause:
But not with the wood that is in the storage area.
phrases.notes: Quoting the end of the משנה.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said: That is to say,
One may not begin using a storeroom in the first place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of רב כהנא's teaching from Step 12. It is based on the סיפא and reaches the opposite rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not begin using a storeroom (אוצר) on יום טוב.

steps.title: In this version the משנה follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה forbids starting a storeroom, its author must be רבי יהודה, who holds of מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is this? It is רבי יהודה, who holds that there is מוקצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks who wrote the משנה according to this version. It answers that the author is רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Forbidding a storeroom means treating stored items as set aside (מוקצה). רבי יהודה holds that rule, and רבי שמעון does not. So in this version the author is רבי יהודה. This is the reverse of Step 13, which named רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is it? Whose opinion is this משנה?
Items set aside from use, which may not be handled on שבת or יום טוב

phrases.english: Whose opinion is it? It is Rabbi Yehuda,
who holds of muktze.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Names the author of the משנה based on the rule in Step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whose opinion does the משנה follow in this version?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה, who holds of מוקצה.

steps.title: But the beginning of the משנה sounds like רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The beginning of the משנה allows starting a straw pile, which sounds like רבי שמעון, who does not hold of מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Look at the first part of the משנה: 'One may begin taking from a pile of straw.' That brings us to רבי שמעון, who does not hold of מוקצה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the claim that the משנה follows רבי יהודה. The first part of the משנה seems to follow רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pile of straw is also stored away, like a storeroom. If the משנה lets you start using it, the משנה seems to ignore מוקצה, which is רבי שמעון's view. Then the beginning and the end of one משנה would follow two different תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part (opening clause) of a משנה
We have come to (the opinion of)
He does not hold of (this rule)

phrases.english: Say the first clause: One may begin with a pile of straw,

phrases.aramaic: אֲתָאן לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן דְּלֵית לֵיהּ מוּקְצֶה!
phrases.english: so we have come to Rabbi Shimon, who does not hold of muktze!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks Step 17's claim that רבי יהודה is the author, using the רישא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Allowing a person to start a stored straw pile goes against מוקצה, so the רישא matches רבי שמעון. That would split the משנה between two authors.

steps.title: The straw is rotten
steps.stepSummary: The straw pile in the משנה is rotten straw that is unfit for animals, so even רבי יהודה agrees it is not מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the משנה is talking about straw that has rotted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the straw pile in the משנה is special. It is rotten straw.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally straw is stored as animal food, so רבי יהודה would call it מוקצה. Rotten straw is no good for animals, so the owner plans to burn it as fuel. Since it is not really 'stored away,' even רבי יהודה lets you use it, and the whole משנה can follow him.

keyTerms.meaning: There (in that other case or clause)

phrases.english: There, it is dealing with rotten straw.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 18 by narrowing the case in the רישא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case limitation (אוקימתא): the straw is a special kind.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The straw pile is ordinary straw stored for animals, so allowing it would go against רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The straw is rotten and is only meant for burning, so even רבי יהודה allows it.

steps.title: But rotten straw is still good for clay
steps.stepSummary: Rotten straw can still be mixed into clay for bricks, so it is still stored for a purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rotten straw? But it is still good for mixing into clay!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. Rotten straw still has another use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in Step 19 assumed that rotten straw can only be burned. But people mixed straw into clay to make bricks. If the owner might save it for that, it is still stored away, and רבי יהודה would call it מוקצה.

phrases.english: Rotten straw? But it is fit for clay!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in Step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that rotten straw is meant only for burning.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Rotten straw still has a use (clay for bricks), so it may still be stored away and count as מוקצה for רבי יהודה.

steps.title: The straw has thorns
steps.stepSummary: The straw has thorns, so it cannot be kneaded into clay and is only good for burning.
steps.simpleTranslation: The straw has thorns in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this straw also has thorns, so nobody would use it for clay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Thorny straw cannot be kneaded by hand into clay. It is no good for animals and no good for bricks, so its only use is fuel. It is clearly not stored away, so even רבי יהודה allows it, and the whole משנה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.whatToRemember: In the second version, רב כהנא learns from the wood clause that one may NOT begin using a storeroom on יום טוב, and the whole משנה follows רבי יהודה. The straw pile is allowed only because it is rotten and thorny, so it is fit only for burning.

phrases.english: That has thorns in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 20 by narrowing the case of the straw further.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Further case limitation: the straw is thorny as well as rotten.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Rotten straw might be saved for making clay, so it is still stored away.
steps.terutzMaskana: The straw has thorns, so it cannot be used for clay. Its only use is fuel, and it is not מוקצה even for רבי יהודה.
